what: DERIVATION, independent attempt 2 of 4: Is the tight-sibling lemma's hypothesis ever satisfied?. GIVEN (refereed censuses): on every small window examined (2x2x2, 3x2x2, the isolated depth-2 cone, the named witnesses) a processed site never has ALL its 1-predecessors tight; the lemma's conclusion was therefore never tested. CAUTION from the referee: probes/lib/family.py's brute_min omits the definition's level restriction (nodes at levels <= level(z)); use probes/lib/rooted.py or restrict it yourself, and for windows with several seeds the single-seed dynamic program gives only upper bounds. TASK: prove or refute: a processed site with at least two processed 1-predecessors cannot have all of them tight (rooted value 0). If true the open lemma of block 33 (PR #8177) is vacuous-true and the unit budget c* = 1 follows (threshold 453 by that route; note the refinement-history route already gives 84). Route: a tight processed site forces a specific local pattern of marks below it (characterize all tight sites at depth <= 3 exhaustively with the correct definition), and two such patterns cannot share the cone of a common successor. ROUND 2: the first round's attempts and referee reports are under probes/work/derive/<problem>/ and logs/probes/J:derive:*/ and logs/probes/J:confirm:J-derive-*/ (python3 probes/harvest.py lists them); what survived refereeing is stated below as GIVEN, what failed is stated as the gap. DELIVERABLE, in your unit worktree on ai/probes: probes/work/derive/tight-sibling-vacuity/<your worker name>/ATTEMPT.md and check.py. ATTEMPT.md: (1) the exact statement you attempt; (2) numbered steps, each marked PROVED (argument given in full), CHECKED (a finite fact check.py verifies exactly) or ASSUMED; (3) if the route fails, the FIRST step that fails and why: a precise no-go for a route is a result; (4) what would finish it. check.py: exact arithmetic (fractions, integers, sympy) for every finite claim; it prints `SUMMARY: PROVED ...`, `SUMMARY: COUNTEREXAMPLE ...`, `SUMMARY: PARTIAL <what is new and exact>` or `SUMMARY: ROUTE FAILS AT <step>`, and a line `HIT: <the claim>` ONLY when you claim a proof, a counterexample, or a new exact partial result others can build on; a HIT is handed to a worker of another model family to referee line by line, so write for a hostile reader. Rules: definitions come from the notes on the PR branches named above (git fetch origin <branch>; git show origin/<branch>:<note>; find them with gh pr view <n> --json files,headRefName); any outside theorem you use must be re-proved at the scope you use it or listed under ASSUMED; no status words (proved theorems are promoted by the supervisor after the referee). Have your own plan BEFORE reading the prior attempts printed at claim time; then either build on a refereed partial result or take a different route. Run: python3 probes/run_probe.py <task> --worker <name> --model <model> --review "..." --extra "python3 probes/work/derive/tight-sibling-vacuity/<name>/check.py"
